subject.title: feat: add jsonl support to memory indexer

question: Should builtin `memorySearch.extraPaths` support arbitrary raw JSONL logs, or should raw message-log ingestion stay in QMD, a converter, or a plugin-owned workflow?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but adding raw JSONL ingestion changes memory semantics and sensitive-data exposure, while VISION.md and AGENTS.md both push optional and storage-sensitive capability toward explicit owner boundaries.

options.title: Require maintainer design first
options.body: Keep this issue open and do not queue automation until maintainers pick builtin support versus QMD/converter/plugin ownership and define the security/read behavior.

options.title: Approve builtin JSONL ingestion
options.body: A future implementation should include line-based parsing, line-map-aware chunks, watcher coverage, `memory_get` behavior, docs, regression tests, and redaction/security expectations.

options.title: Document external workflow
options.body: If arbitrary raw logs are out of scope for builtin memory, document QMD extra collections or a converter/plugin pattern and then close this issue against that decision.

recommendation.title: Require maintainer design first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and do not queue automation until maintainers pick builtin support versus QMD/converter/plugin ownership and define the security/read behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already left the current maintainer-side keep-open analysis and is tied to the memory-engine refactor history.
